state: Can compiles to TypeScript executed on pinned Bun 1.4.2. B1-11 adds typed decoders for TOML, YAML, JSON5 and JSONL. The established codec pipeline is schema-first: the checker derives a CodecSchema graph (primitives str, int, float, bool plus arrays, records, errors and variants) from the target type, the emitter instantiates one factory per specialization, and the adapter parses the input bytes::buffer under standaloneBytes, maxDepth and maxNodes caps, then projects native values into immutable Can records and arrays. Every projection failure becomes codec::invalid_data with a safe path and a reason such as missing_member, extra_member, type, integer_token, nonfinite or duplicate_member. The existing decode_json path keeps exact integers by replaying native numeric tokens. Pinned probes of the new parsers observe: Bun.TOML.parse rejects 9007199254740993 with a losslessness SyntaxError and rejects redefined keys, while Bun.YAML.parse and Bun.JSON5.parse silently round 9007199254740993 to 9007199254740992 and keep the last of duplicate keys; all three return genuine NaN and Infinity numbers for their nonfinite spellings; Bun.TOML.parse yields Temporal objects (PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainTime, Instant) for dates while YAML timestamps stay plain strings; YAML follows YAML 1.2 core typing (yes and on remain strings, null forms become null), resolves merge keys, shares aliased nodes by identity, can return a genuinely cyclic object for a self-referential anchor, and returns an array of documents for multi-document input; TOML requires a table root and accepts mixed arrays; Bun.JSONL.parse rounds 9007199254740993 to 9007199254740992, skips blank lines, accepts CRLF and a final line without a newline, accepts records spanning several lines, and on trailing garbage silently returns only the valid prefix with no error and no consumed-byte count; Bun.JSONL.parseChunk reports values, read, done and error per call. Adapter rules: reuse native parsers only, no adapter-side document grammar; numeric exactness is an explicit contract choice per format, never a postprocessing claim; duplicate rejection stays available only where native metadata supports it.

naming.instructions: How should the new document decoders be named in the catalogue?

criteria.codec_prefixed: One codec domain keeps every decoder: codec::decode_toml, codec::decode_yaml, codec::decode_json5 and JSONL siblings, mirroring the existing decode_json generic shape.
criteria.format_domains: Each format owns a domain with a short verb: toml::decode, yaml::decode, json5::decode and jsonl::decode with jsonl::consume, matching the contract sketch.
criteria.single_decode: A single generic codec::decode takes a format tag plus the buffer, so one operation covers every format through a runtime switch.

jsonl_strictness.instructions: Which JSONL decoding semantics should the contract promise?

criteria.framed_exact: Strict line framing plus the exact JSON record path: blank lines skipped, CRLF and unterminated final lines accepted, multi-line records rejected, unsafe integers preserved, truncated input fails.
criteria.native_whole: Whole-input Bun.JSONL.parse: multi-line records accepted, unsafe integers round, trailing garbage silently returns the valid prefix.
criteria.framed_native: Line framing for record boundaries with native JSON values per line: multi-line records rejected, unsafe integers still round.

toml_dates.instructions: How should TOML temporal values cross into Can?

criteria.reject_dates: Temporal objects are unsupported input: any PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainTime or Instant fails the projection with codec::invalid_data.
criteria.project_instant: Offset datetimes project onto time::instant handles while local dates, times and datetimes without zone fail as unsupported.
criteria.project_string: Every temporal object stringifies to ISO text and projects as an ordinary str, leaving interpretation to Can code.
